Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Zhao heard of it and memorialized to admonish the emperor, asking that he draw near teachers, extend inquiry to upright men, and open his intelligence.
聞之，上疏諫帝，請：「親近師傅，延問正人，以開聰明」 requires hearing of it, a memorial of admonition, and the three-part request; the prior idiomatic truncates that content and ends with a stray closing quote.

As Yun traveled to Songzhou, Taizu from Chanzhou was forced back to the capital by soldiers; Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with seven hundred horse to guard Yun.
赟行至宋州 is Yun reaching Songzhou, while 太祖自澶州為兵士擁還京師 is Taizu forced back from Chanzhou; 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Dazhou, and the prior line reverses those subjects.

As Yun traveled to Songzhou, Taizu from Dazhou was forced back to the capital by soldiers; Wang Jun feared Yun’s attendants might stir trouble and sent palace guard horse commander Guo Chong with seven hundred cavalry to escort Yun.

As Yun traveled to Songzhou, Taizu from Chanzhou was forced back to the capital by soldiers; Wang Jun feared Yun’s attendants might stir trouble and sent palace guard horse commander Guo Chong with seven hundred cavalry to escort Yun.
自澶州 names Chanzhou; Dazhou is a wrong romanization of 澶州, and the rest of the literal already tracks the Chinese.
Chong came; Yun asked why; Chong said Dazhou had mutinied and he came to protect him, not harm him.”
Chong came; Yun asked why; Chong said Chanzhou had mutinied and he came to protect him, not harm him.
崇曰：「澶州軍變」 refers to mutiny at Chanzhou, not Dazhou; the prior idiomatic also ends with a stray unmatched closing quote.
When Chong reached Songzhou, Yun ascended a tower and asked Chong’s purpose; Chong said: “There was mutiny at Dazhou; fearing matters were unclear, he was sent to guard—no ill intent.”
When Chong reached Songzhou, Yun ascended a tower and asked Chong’s purpose; Chong said: “There was mutiny at Chanzhou; fearing matters were unclear, he was sent to guard—no ill intent.”
In Chong’s speech 澶州軍變 is Chanzhou; replacing Dazhou with Chanzhou corrects the place name without other changes.
When Guo Wei's army mutinied at Dazhou, Wang Jun sent the former prefect of Shenzhou, Ma Duo, to inspect Xu with troops; Xin then killed himself.
When Guo Wei's army mutinied at Chanzhou, Wang Jun sent the former prefect of Shenzhou, Ma Duo, to inspect Xu with troops; Xin then killed himself.
周太祖軍變於澶州 places the mutiny at Chanzhou; Dazhou misreads 澶州, and the rest of the idiomatic line is otherwise sound.
When Taizu of Zhou's army mutinied at Dazhou, Wang Jun sent former prefect of Shenzhou Ma Duo with troops to inspect Xu; Xin then killed himself.
When Taizu of Zhou's army mutinied at Chanzhou, Wang Jun sent former prefect of Shenzhou Ma Duo with troops to inspect Xu; Xin then killed himself.
The literal’s Dazhou is the same 澶州 error; Chanzhou is the correct reading for the mutiny place.

After their deaths, Taizu of Zhou marched on the capital; Murong Yanchao was defeated at Liuzipo; the emperor meant to take the field himself; the dowager stopped him: “Guo Wei was originally one of our household—had he not been driven to doubt, how would he have come to this!
周太祖 and 慕容彥超 should be Taizu of Zhou and Murong Yanchao; 敗於 is defeat, not falling dead; and 本吾家人，非其危疑，何肯至此！ is the dowager’s counterfactual, which the prior speech shortens.
